name: Trinity Church
description: An Episcopal church on Copley Square with massive proportions, rounded arches, and rough rock-faced, multicolored stone. The interior decoration was the work of painter John La Farge and his team, and the stained glass windows were produced by nine different studios, including works by William Morris and Edward Burne-Jones. It is home to an active parish and is not a museum.
significance_text: Constructed and decorated between 1872 and 1877, it is the prototype of the style that became known as Richardsonian Romanesque. It was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1971, and the church states that the American Institute of Architects has recognized it as one of the ten most important buildings in America.

admission.notes: Open for tours Tuesday through Saturday from 10 am to 4:30 pm. Adults $10. Seniors, students, educators, military, first responders, and Massachusetts residents $8. Children younger than 14 and EBT and WIC cardholders are free. Tickets include a self-guided, audio, or guided tour and are bought on arrival at the Welcome Desk. On Tuesdays admission pauses from 12:00 pm to 12:45 pm. Hours may vary due to weddings, funerals, and worship services.
